draft.title: The founding of Rome
card: Rome began as a group of small villages on hills beside the Tiber River in central Italy. Over time the villages joined together to form one city.
The site suited a settlement. The river gave fresh water and a way to travel and trade, and the hills were good places to defend.
a story passed down over time that people tell about the past. It may have some truth in it, but it is not proven history.
Romans told a legend that twin brothers, Romulus and Remus, founded their city. In the story, Romulus became its first king and the city was named after him.
draft.remember: Rome grew from villages by the Tiber River, and Romans explained its start with the legend of Romulus and Remus.

a.q: Which statement about the founding of Rome is best supported by the card?
opts: Rome grew from small villages beside the Tiber River
Rome was built in a single year by Romulus and Remus
Rome began as a port city on the coast of Greece
Rome was founded after a republic replaced its kings
a.why: The card says Rome began as small villages by the Tiber River in Italy that joined into one city. The legend names twin founders, but it is a story and not proven history, so it cannot be treated as a fact about who built the city.
a.clue: Think about what actually grew into the city, not the story told about it.

b.q: A student says, 'Romulus and Remus really did found Rome, because Romans told this story for hundreds of years.' Why is this reasoning weak?
opts: A legend can hold some truth but is not proven history
A story cannot be about real places such as the Tiber
Romans did not tell any stories about their origins
Legends are always made up and have no link to the past
b.why: A legend is a story told about the past. It may have some truth in it, but being told for a long time does not prove it happened. The last option goes too far, because the card says a legend may contain some truth.
b.clue: Does telling a story for a long time make it proven?

wants.brief: A simple map of central Italy showing the Tiber River and the site of Rome on it, with the hills marked near the river.
wants.why: It shows how the river and hills made a good place for villages to grow into a city.

a.best: Rome grew from small villages beside the Tiber River

b.best: A legend can hold some truth but is not proven history
